newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen accepts IMF obligations on payment reforms.
newsitem.headline: Yemen accepts IMF obligations on payment reforms.

text.p: Yemen has accepted obligations with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to establish current account convertability and an open foreign exchange, an official said on Friday.

Yemen would adhere to IMF's Article VIII, undertaking to refrain from restricting international current payments or from engaging in discriminatory currency arrangements or multiple currency rates without IMF approval with effect from December 10, 1996, the official told Reuters.
Yemen, a small oil producer, is an impoverished Arab country suffering from about 25 percent unemployment.
It has received soft loans from several countries and international organisations under its reform plan that has included raising the prices of fuel and electricity and water and telephones rates.
